samples.summary: The `fullSettled`-on-failure branch (a failed full-catalog load must still unblock recent rows) has no test
samples.evidence: `.finally(() => setFullSettled(true))` plus `previewable = entry !== undefined || fullSettled` is a new, explicitly documented branch: on load FAILURE the row must still become observable and preview at default weights. The only stub of `loadFullFontCatalog` in `font-family-picker.test.ts:32-48` always RESOLVES, so the rejection path is never driven — the `.catch()`/`.finally()` combination could be deleted (leaving the row permanently unpreviewable) and every test would stay green. I grepped the frontend tests for `loadFullFontCatalog` (only the resolving mock and `font-catalog-full-loader.test.ts`, which tests the loader itself, not the picker's failure handling) and for `reject`/`mockRejected` in the text-formatting tests: nothing.

samples.summary: `needFullForRecents` guard (don't pull the 1,900-entry library when every recent is curated) is untested
samples.evidence: The new trigger `if (!moreOpen && !(open && needFullForRecents)) return;` is only ever exercised in its TRUE direction (the recents test seeds an off-catalog family). No test asserts the load is skipped when all recents are curated, and the mock is a plain factory function rather than a `vi.fn()`, so call counts cannot be asserted at all — inverting the guard to always fetch would keep the suite green. Searched font-family-picker.test.ts for any assertion on load invocation.

samples.summary: Test titled "design-editor:build produces what its exports map names" only string-matches the script name; it cannot detect an emit-path change
samples.evidence: The assertions are `assert.match(pkg.exports['.'].default, /^\.\/dist\//)` and `assert.ok(pkg.scripts.build.includes('build:plugin'))`. Neither connects `build:plugin` to the path `exports` names: `build:plugin` is `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`, whose `outDir: dist` + `rootDir: src` + `include: src/plugin/**` is what actually puts the file at `dist/plugin/index.js`. Change the outDir (or `exports` to `./dist/whatever.js`) and the test still passes while every consumer breaks — exactly the failure the test claims to guard. The title over-claims relative to what is asserted.

samples.summary: New two-artefact mtime staleness logic added in three scripts (plus scripts/design.mjs) with no test anywhere
samples.evidence: `buildIfStale` (verify-consumer.mjs), `buildDesignEditorIfStale` (verify-scenes.mjs and verify-tokens.mjs) and the `EDITOR_DIST`/`newestSrc` comparison in scripts/design.mjs are four near-identical new copies of gate logic whose whole point is 'a gate that can pass on stale bytes is worse than no gate'. None of them is on CI by the diff's own admission, and `scripts/test/` (agent-workflow-guards, ci-workflow, changed-areas, verify-doc-index, failure-summary, verify-entropy, verify-doc-links, design-pr, verify-self-lanes) contains no test for design.mjs's staleness computation or for the package scripts — so a regression (e.g. dropping `dist/plugin/index.js` from the list again, or the `<` vs `<=` mismatch between the two copies) is caught by nothing. `design-pr.test.mjs` shows scripts of this kind are testable in this repo.

samples.summary: Per-character `toContain` loop is a weak substitute for asserting the subset set
samples.evidence: `for (const ch of "LobsterDisplay") expect(text).toContain(ch)` passes for any superset of those glyphs in any order and does not pin the de-duplication/ordering contract the unit test elsewhere asserts exactly (`text=Waflebs FkOn`). It does discriminate label-only subsetting (D/y come only from "Display"), so it is not vacuous — just looser than it reads.

samples.summary: `previewWeight`'s empty-spec fallback is untested and silently returns TWO cuts
samples.evidence: `first || DEFAULT_WEIGHTS` returns `'400;700'` when the weights string is empty/whitespace, contradicting the function's documented 'single weight a preview requests'. Tests in ensure-font-link.test.ts cover `'700'`, `'300;400;700'` and the undefined/catalog paths, but never `''` or `'  '`, so that branch has no coverage.

searchedFor: grep verify:fast in scripts/ for a lane/script parity test
finding.summary: The new `design-editor:build` prerequisite edges (entropy + design-sandbox) have no test pinning them; only self-consistent generic checks exist
finding.evidence: This delta exists to fix a concrete failure: an unbuilt `packages/design-editor/dist` made `verify:entropy` die with `Could not parse knip output as JSON` and made `design-sandbox:check`'s tsc fail. The fix is entirely lane-graph data (`needs: [... "design-editor:build"]` in verify-self.mjs, entropy at ~line 452 and design-sandbox:check at ~line 380). The only tests over that data are in scripts/test/verify-self-lanes.test.mjs, and both relevant ones are self-consistent rather than fact-pinning: "a selected lane never runs without its prerequisites" (line 211) only walks the `needs` a lane already declares, and "a design-editor change runs its check AND the knip gate" (line 165) asserts `design-editor:check`, `design-sandbox:check`, `verify:entropy` and `core:build` but never `design-editor:build`. So deleting `"design-editor:build"` from entropy's or design-sandbox's `needs` — the exact regression this PR repairs — keeps the whole suite green, and the failure returns as an opaque knip/JSON error. The file already demonstrates the fact-pinning style it omits here (line 123 explicitly asserts `core:build` is pulled in by entropy's needs; line 145 asserts the same for frontend), so a matching assertion is cheap and clearly in the file's remit.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists in the exact file the finding names. scripts/test/verify-self-lanes.test.mjs:94-112 is a subtest, "every lane that loads design-editor's dist declares its build", that loops over ["design-editor:check", "design-sandbox:check", "verify:entropy"] and asserts each lane's needs includes "design-editor:build" (line 108). Its comment (lines 96-101) explicitly states the reviewer's own rationale — that the generic prerequisite walk is self-consistent and would pass if the edge were deleted — which is why this by-name pin exists. Deleting "design-editor:build" from verify:entropy's needs (scripts/verify-self.mjs:458-464) or design-sandbox:check's needs (scripts/verify-self.mjs:370) fails this assertion, contradicting the claim that "the whole suite stays green". Additionally lines 228-231 pin the same edge at the selection altitude, and lines 114-126 pin that the build lane actually emits the exports["."] dist path. Assertions run against the real lane array via `node scripts/verify-self.mjs --print-lanes` (test lines 29-34; emitter at scripts/verify-self.mjs:654-664, which includes `needs`), and the file is executed by the scripts:tests lane globbing scripts/test/**/*.test.mjs (scripts/verify-self.mjs:180-181). The finding's cited line numbers (165, 211, 123, 145) do not match the working tree (the design-editor selection test is at line 200, the generic walk at 253), indicating it was written against a pre-fix revision.
